mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased production costs, negatively impacting corporate profit margins and thus S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where RSAFS shows a sustained increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) signals a slowdown in economic activity, which can lead to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases > 1% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and CPIAUCSL is increasing, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy environment combined with inflationary pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased production costs, negatively impacting corporate profit margins and thus S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k in 1 month and UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS increases > 200k in 1 month and UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) signals a strong demand for housing, which boosts related industries and the overall economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST increases > 10% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth slows down and Industrial Production (INDPRO) decreases, it indicates a broad economic slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 2% YoY and INDPRO decreases > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 growth < 2% YoY and INDPRO decreases > 1% in 1 month.
